summary: Frontend-only verification of iteration 52 features. All 6 requested features verified end-to-end against the live preview URL. (1) Shared AppearanceControls on /app workspace: theme-toggle + font-size-toggle render on the authenticated TabBar, theme flips light↔dark on <html data-theme>, font-size-menu opens with sm/md/lg options, outside-click closes menu. (2) Pricing dark-mode contrast: Student/Starter/Research/Professional/pro_monthly/lab_team plan titles AND prices all resolve to rgb(237,234,251) (= #EDEAFB) in dark mode. Research 'Most Popular' card background gradient resolves to linear-gradient(rgb(42,34,56), rgb(26,21,51)) — dark surface — so the lifted ink stays legible. (3) Bulk Docking Select All/None on /dock: both dock-comp-select-all/none and dock-tgt-select-all/none buttons present and functional. (4) dock-batch-summary panel renders above Vina params with exact text 'Batch: N compound(s) × M target(s) = N*M docking pair(s)' and updates live as checkboxes toggle. (5) Auto-select on /dock Load: 5 compounds + 3 targets → ALL 5 compounds and ALL 3 targets pre-checked (no 3-cap in standalone). (6) Regression: public SiteHeader theme-toggle + font-size menu work on /, /pricing, /plant-database, /documentation — theme flips both ways, menu opens and closes via outside-click.
critical_code_review_comments: AppearanceControls.jsx is a clean refactor — single source of truth for the theme+font-size cluster, capture-phase mousedown handler encapsulated, dark/compact variants via props. Good move.

MolecularDocking.jsx selection panel: dock-batch-summary only renders when (selectedComp.length > 0 || selectedGenes.length > 0). If a user manually unchecks every compound AND every target the summary disappears — intentional, but may feel abrupt. Minor UX nit, not a bug.

Pricing dark-mode fix appears to be driven by the index.css global dark-remap for #0F172A → light ink (per iteration_51 note) rather than per-card theme-aware tokens. Works correctly now, but the fragile override pattern flagged previously still applies — any new near-black hex utility added to pricing cards would again be unreadable in dark mode.
